stem: Which two protocols transmit credentials in clear text and should be replaced on a modern network? (Choose two.)

options.text: Telnet
SSH
FTP
SFTP
HTTPS

explanation: Telnet and FTP both carry authentication in plain text, so anyone able to observe the traffic reads the credentials. SSH replaces Telnet and SFTP or FTPS replaces FTP.

distractorExplanations.b: SSH encrypts the entire session, which is why it replaced Telnet.
distractorExplanations.d: SFTP runs inside an SSH session and is encrypted.
distractorExplanations.e: HTTPS protects the session with TLS.

stem: A host is configured with 192.168.20.70/26. Which two addresses are valid hosts on the same subnet? (Choose two.)
explanation: A /26 has blocks of 64. The block containing .70 runs from .64 to .127, so its usable range is .65 through .126.

distractorExplanations.c: 192.168.20.64 is the network address of the block and cannot be assigned to a host.
distractorExplanations.d: 192.168.20.127 is the broadcast address of the block.
distractorExplanations.e: 192.168.20.130 falls in the next block, which starts at .128.

stem: Under the shared responsibility model for IaaS, which two tasks belong to the customer? (Choose two.)

options.text: Patching the guest operating system
Configuring security group rules
Securing the hypervisor
Replacing failed physical disks
Maintaining the data center's physical access controls

explanation: In IaaS the provider secures everything up to and including the hypervisor; the customer owns the guest OS and the network policy applied to its instances.

distractorExplanations.c: The hypervisor is part of the infrastructure the provider secures.
distractorExplanations.d: Physical hardware replacement is a provider responsibility.
distractorExplanations.e: Facility security belongs to the provider.

stem: Which two conditions require single-mode fiber rather than multimode? (Choose two.)

options.text: A 20 km run between buildings
A 10 Gbps link that must reach 40 km
A 50 m link between two switches in the same rack row
A 100 m horizontal run to a workstation
A 3 m connection inside a single rack

explanation: Single-mode uses a narrow core and a laser source, which avoids the modal dispersion that limits multimode to a few hundred metres. Distance, not speed alone, is what forces the choice.

distractorExplanations.c: 50 m is comfortably inside multimode's range.
distractorExplanations.d: A 100 m horizontal run is normally copper, and multimode would also serve.
distractorExplanations.e: A 3 m intra-rack link is typically direct attach copper.

stem: Which two conditions must match for a port channel to form between two switches? (Choose two.)

options.text: Speed on every member interface
Duplex on every member interface
Interface descriptions
Switch hostnames
Serial numbers of the two switches

explanation: Aggregation requires consistent Layer 1 and Layer 2 parameters across members; a mismatched interface is excluded from the bundle or prevents it forming.

distractorExplanations.c: Descriptions are cosmetic and never affect negotiation.
distractorExplanations.d: Hostnames play no part in link aggregation.
distractorExplanations.e: Hardware serial numbers are irrelevant to the protocol.

stem: Which two changes reduce co-channel interference in a dense wireless deployment? (Choose two.)

options.text: Reduce transmit power so cells are smaller
Use a repeating 1, 6, 11 channel plan in 2.4 GHz
Increase transmit power on every access point
Widen every channel to 80 MHz in 2.4 GHz
Disable the 5 GHz radio to consolidate clients

explanation: Smaller cells and a non-overlapping channel plan both reduce the number of radios contending for the same airtime, which is what co-channel interference actually is.

distractorExplanations.c: Higher power enlarges cells and makes contention worse.
distractorExplanations.d: 2.4 GHz cannot fit 80 MHz channels without severe overlap.
distractorExplanations.e: Disabling 5 GHz pushes every client into the more congested band.

stem: Which two statements about administrative distance are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: It breaks ties between routes to the same prefix learned from different sources
A lower value is considered more trustworthy
It is compared before longest prefix match
It is exchanged between routers in routing updates
It replaces the protocol metric when comparing two OSPF routes

explanation: Administrative distance ranks the trustworthiness of route sources and is consulted only when the same prefix is learned more than once. Lower wins.

distractorExplanations.c: Longest prefix match is applied first; administrative distance never overrides a more specific route.
distractorExplanations.d: Administrative distance is locally significant and is not advertised.
distractorExplanations.e: Two routes from the same protocol are compared by that protocol's metric.

stem: Which two practices improve airflow in a equipment rack? (Choose two.)

options.text: Installing blanking panels in unused rack units
Arranging racks in hot aisle and cold aisle rows
Mounting the heaviest equipment at the top
Facing every rack in the same direction
Coiling excess patch cable across the intake vents

explanation: Both keep cold intake air and hot exhaust separated: blanking panels stop air bypassing equipment through empty units, and the aisle arrangement stops one rack ingesting another's exhaust.

distractorExplanations.c: Heavy equipment belongs low for stability; this is a safety error, not an airflow one.
distractorExplanations.d: Uniform facing makes each rack breathe the exhaust of the one in front.

stem: An organization sets a four-hour RTO and a 15-minute RPO. Which two measures support meeting them? (Choose two.)

options.text: Replicating data to the recovery site at least every 15 minutes
Maintaining a warm or hot site that can take over within four hours
Increasing the MTBF rating of the production hardware
Extending backup retention to seven years
Scheduling a full backup once per week

explanation: RPO drives replication frequency and RTO drives how ready the recovery site must be. The two metrics are met by different measures, and both are needed.

distractorExplanations.c: A higher MTBF makes failure less frequent but does nothing for recovery speed once it happens.
distractorExplanations.d: Retention governs how far back you can restore, not how much data is lost or how fast service returns.
distractorExplanations.e: A weekly full backup alone implies up to a week of data loss, far outside a 15-minute RPO.

stem: Which two data sources are needed to attribute bandwidth use to a specific host and destination? (Choose two.)

options.text: Flow records exported from the router
A collector that stores and reports on those records
SNMP interface counters alone
The switch's ARP cache
Syslog messages at severity 6

explanation: Flow export produces the per-conversation metadata, but it is only useful once a collector retains and aggregates it. Either half alone answers nothing.

distractorExplanations.c: Interface counters give totals per port and cannot break traffic down by conversation.
distractorExplanations.d: The ARP cache maps addresses on the local segment and carries no volume data.
distractorExplanations.e: Syslog records discrete events, not traffic volume.

stem: Clients on a remote VLAN receive no DHCP addresses while clients on the server's own VLAN work. Which two facts explain why, and what fixes it? (Choose two.)

options.text: DHCP DISCOVER is a broadcast and routers do not forward broadcasts
An IP helper address on the remote VLAN's gateway relays the request as unicast
The scope is too small for the remote VLAN
The lease duration on the server is too long
The remote clients need static reservations to receive any address

explanation: The cause is that the discovery broadcast never leaves the segment; the fix is a relay that converts it to a unicast aimed at the server.

distractorExplanations.c: Scope size is irrelevant when the request never reaches the server.
distractorExplanations.d: Lease duration affects renewal, not initial reachability.
distractorExplanations.e: Reservations still require the request to arrive at the server.

stem: Which two switch features work together to drop forged ARP messages? (Choose two.)

options.text: DHCP snooping
Dynamic ARP inspection
BPDU guard
Storm control
PortFast

explanation: DHCP snooping builds the table of legitimate IP-to-MAC bindings, and dynamic ARP inspection validates ARP traffic against that table. Neither is sufficient alone.

distractorExplanations.c: BPDU guard protects spanning tree from rogue switches.
distractorExplanations.d: Storm control limits excessive broadcast or multicast rates.
distractorExplanations.e: PortFast speeds up port transition for end devices.

stem: Which two examples combine to form genuine multifactor authentication? (Choose two.)

options.text: A password
A hardware token generating a rotating code
A password and a PIN
Two security questions
A username

explanation: Multifactor requires factors from different categories. A password is something you know and a token is something you have; together they qualify.

distractorExplanations.c: A password and a PIN are both something you know, so this is single-factor twice over.
distractorExplanations.d: Security questions are also knowledge factors.
distractorExplanations.e: A username is an identifier, not an authentication factor.

stem: An attacker floods a switch with frames from thousands of random source MAC addresses. Which two outcomes follow? (Choose two.)

options.text: The CAM table fills and cannot record legitimate entries
The switch floods unknown unicast frames out all ports
The DHCP scope is exhausted
The routing table is overwritten
Spanning tree elects a new root bridge

explanation: MAC flooding exhausts the CAM table so the switch fails open, flooding frames it can no longer map to a port. That flooding is what lets the attacker capture traffic.

distractorExplanations.c: Exhausting addresses is DHCP starvation, a different attack.
distractorExplanations.d: The routing table is a Layer 3 structure unaffected by CAM exhaustion.
distractorExplanations.e: A root bridge election requires crafted BPDUs.

stem: An interface on a full-duplex link shows rising CRC errors. Which two causes are consistent with that symptom? (Choose two.)

options.text: A damaged or poorly terminated cable
Electromagnetic interference along the run
An undersized DHCP scope
An incorrect VLAN assignment on the port
A default gateway misconfigured on the host

explanation: A CRC error means the frame arrived corrupted, which is a physical layer symptom. On a full-duplex link, collisions are ruled out, leaving the medium itself.

distractorExplanations.c: Address exhaustion prevents hosts obtaining addresses; it does not corrupt frames.
distractorExplanations.d: A VLAN error isolates traffic rather than damaging it.
distractorExplanations.e: A gateway error breaks reachability without affecting frame integrity.

stem: A user can reach a server by IP but not by name. Which two commands help isolate the fault? (Choose two.)

options.text: nslookup
dig
iperf
arp -a
ipconfig /release

explanation: Reaching the host by address proves connectivity, so the fault is in resolution. Both tools query DNS directly and report which server answered and with what record.

distractorExplanations.d: arp shows local address mappings, which are already working.
distractorExplanations.e: Releasing the address discards a working configuration and tests nothing.

stem: A file transfer over a WAN link achieves far less than the circuit's capacity, with low utilization and no errors. Which two factors should be examined? (Choose two.)

options.text: Round trip time on the path
The TCP window size in use
The number of VLANs configured along the path
The DHCP lease duration on both hosts
The spanning tree root bridge location

explanation: A single TCP session is bounded by window size divided by round trip time. On a long path, an undersized window leaves most of the circuit idle no matter how much capacity exists.

distractorExplanations.c: VLAN count does not constrain per-session throughput.
distractorExplanations.d: Lease duration is an addressing parameter.
distractorExplanations.e: Root bridge placement affects Layer 2 topology, not TCP windowing.

stem: A technician has confirmed a theory of probable cause. Which two steps come next, in order, before the work is complete? (Choose two.)

options.text: Establish a plan of action and implement the solution
Verify full system functionality and document the outcome
Establish a new theory of probable cause
Escalate to a higher support tier
Question the obvious and gather symptoms

explanation: Once the cause is confirmed the methodology moves to planning and implementing the fix, then to verifying the whole system and documenting what was found and done.

distractorExplanations.c: A new theory is needed only when the first is disproved.
distractorExplanations.d: Escalation applies when the cause cannot be determined.
distractorExplanations.e: Gathering symptoms belongs to the identification step, which is already finished.
